r7-resume.title: "Where was I?": pick up where you left off
body: Getting back into something after a break is often the hardest part of the day. When you unlock Shiftbook, a card at the top of the Desk shows the last thing you worked on, its tickets and its next step. **Carry on** puts it straight into Log work.

Every entry already has a hidden **next step** field, so this mostly shows what's already saved. It pairs with the wrap-up card above: what you write in "tomorrow I start with…" is what this card shows the next morning.
bullets: Shows only after a lock, a break of 30 minutes or more, or a new day. Never in the middle of work.
**Later** hides it until the next unlock. With nothing to pick up, it doesn't appear at all.
The entry's details panel gets a **Next step** box, so you can fill it in as you go.

figures.caption: Switch between "Back from lunch" and "Next morning" at the top, then press Carry on. Made-up data.

r7-timer.title: A soft "now doing" timer for when you lose track of time
body: Press **▶ Start** on an entry and a small clock sits at the top of the window. Press **Stop** and Shiftbook offers to add the time, rounded to 15 minutes. You always choose; nothing is added on its own.
It keeps the rule you set at the start: **only minutes are saved**, never start or end times. If you walked away while it ran, it notices the quiet time and suggests leaving that out.
bullets: One timer at a time. Starting another asks to stop the first.
Locking the app or the computer sleeping pauses it.
Hyperfocus-friendly: no alarms or pop-ups while it runs, only the clock.

figures.caption: Press ▶ Start, wait a few seconds (the clock runs 60× fast), then press "Pretend I walked away" and Stop.

r7-next.title: What's unfinished, and what I'd build next
body: I went through the alpha looking for things that are half built. The full list is in the project files (*unfinished-and-ideas.md*). These are the big ones, in the order I'd take them. Search and the greyed-out views are already on cards above, so they're not repeated here.
bullets: **Backups.** There are none yet. If the database file is lost or damaged, everything is gone. Encrypted `.shiftbak` backups (automatic, plus Backup now and Restore) were always planned as a must.
**Recurring work and Due soon.** The rules (next due, days left, overdue, routine items) are written and tested, and the table exists. It needs saving, a screen and the Due soon panel on the Desk.
**Project budgets and alerts.** Hours left, % of estimate used, Over budget and Overdue are worked out already; projects only show a name and colour today.
**Tasks.** The table and the overdue rule exist; there's no list or board yet.
**Ctrl+Shift+Space from anywhere.** Approved in round 2; capture only works while Shiftbook is in front.

r7-weekstart.title: Done: your week can start on any day
body: The week always started on Monday. Now **Customize → Timesheet** has **My week starts on**. The ribbon, the crib sheet and words like "next week" in capture all follow it. It's in a draft pull request, waiting for your OK.

figures.caption: The new setting at the bottom of Customize → Timesheet. Screenshot of the real app with made-up data.
With Sunday picked, each block on the ribbon runs Sunday to Saturday (this week is 11 to 17 October).

r7-backups.title: Backups: automatic, Back up now and Restore
body: You picked backups next, so they're built. **Customize → Backups** is a new section. Shiftbook saves a backup on its own once a day when you unlock it, and keeps the last 14. **Back up now…** saves one wherever you like, such as a USB stick.

**Restore…** works on any backup in the list, or on a file you pick. First it shows what the backup holds and asks you to confirm. Your data as it is right then is saved first, so a restore can always be undone. Every backup is locked with your password, like the data itself. It's in a draft pull request, waiting for your OK.
bullets: A backup made on this computer opens without asking for your password again.
A backup from another computer, or from before Delete all data, asks for the password or recovery key from when it was made.
Still to do later: a backup when you close Shiftbook, and choosing how many to keep.

figures.caption: Restoring a backup from the list: what it holds, and the warning that today's data is saved first. Made-up data.
Restoring a file from another computer: it asks for the password or recovery key it was made with.
